svg.text: Charged particles in a magnetic field and the velocity selector
only v = E/B passes straight; others are deflected

g.text: force on a moving charge: F = q v x B, F = qvB sin theta (10.14); it is always at right angles to v, so it changes the direction
of motion but not the speed or kinetic energy; across a uniform field the path is a circle: qvB = mv^2/r gives r = mv/(qB)
velocity selector: a parallel plate capacitor (field E) inside a magnetic field B at right angles; for a charge moving across both,
the magnetic force Bqv and the electric force qE are opposite, and they balance when Bqv = qE, that is v = E/B (10.15)
Ex 10.4: alpha particles of 1000 to 2000 m s^-1, E = 300 V m^-1, B = 0.20 T: only 1500 m s^-1 passes undeviated
Ex 10.5: E = 4.8 x 10^3 N C^-1, B = 0.2 T, radius 3.0 cm with E off: q/m = E/(B^2 r) = 4 x 10^6 C kg^-1
a charge moving along the field feels no magnetic force; a magnet near an old TV or oscilloscope screen bends the electron beam
